sourcesNote: Official names, descriptions and grades follow the GTA VI trophy list as published by Exophase and PSNProfiles before launch; the two lists agree on every name, description and grade. Guides are written in our own words from those official descriptions. Where a location, step or trigger is not pinned down by the description or a cited source, the guide says so instead of guessing.

trophies.name: Vice Got a Price!
trophies.missable_note: Not missable. It unlocks automatically once the other 54 trophies are earned, in any order.
trophies.guide: The platinum. Earn the other 54 trophies — every story chapter, every activity, every collectible set — and this unlocks on its own. There is no separate task behind it, so treat it as a progress check, not a goal to chase directly. Follow the roadmap in order: story first, then activities, then collectibles, then the 100% cleanup for A Long Road.
steps: Earn all 54 other trophies in any order.
This trophy unlocks automatically when the last one lands.

trophies.name: Just Like Paradise
trophies.missable_note: Tied to the opening mission. Whether story missions can be replayed after the story moves on is not yet checked in the game — finish it as it comes.
trophies.guide: Complete the opening mission, Gone Fishing. This is the first story mission of the game, so it unlocks naturally as you start playing — no detour needed. If you are following the story, you cannot miss the mission itself; the only open question is whether it can be replayed later, which has not yet been checked in the game.
steps: Start a new game and play the opening mission, Gone Fishing, to its end.
The trophy unlocks when the mission completes.

trophies.name: Paradise Lost
trophies.missable_note: Tied to a story chapter. Whether chapters can be replayed is not yet checked in the game — finish the chapter as it comes.
trophies.guide: Complete Chapter 1 of the story. Play through the chapter's missions in order; the trophy unlocks when the final mission of the chapter ends and the chapter closes. No side content is needed for it — it is a pure story-progress trophy.
steps: Play the story missions of Chapter 1 in order.
The trophy unlocks when the chapter's final mission completes.

trophies.name: T**s Ass Drug Money
trophies.missable_note: Tied to a story chapter. Whether chapters can be replayed is not yet checked in the game — finish the chapter as it comes.
trophies.guide: Complete Chapter 2 of the story. Like every chapter trophy, it unlocks when the chapter's final mission ends — just keep playing the main story in order. The name is the official trophy name exactly as listed by Exophase and PSNProfiles, asterisks included.
steps: Play the story missions of Chapter 2 in order.
The trophy unlocks when the chapter's final mission completes.

trophies.name: Vice City, Baby!
trophies.missable_note: Tied to a story chapter. Whether chapters can be replayed is not yet checked in the game — finish the chapter as it comes.
trophies.guide: Complete Chapter 3 of the story. The trophy is awarded for story progress alone: finish the chapter's missions in order and it unlocks at the chapter's close. Use the chapters as natural stopping points — each one is a clean save-and-check moment for your progress.
steps: Play the story missions of Chapter 3 in order.
The trophy unlocks when the chapter's final mission completes.

trophies.name: Top Of The World, Ma
trophies.missable_note: Tied to a story chapter. Whether chapters can be replayed is not yet checked in the game — finish the chapter as it comes.
trophies.guide: Complete Chapter 4 of the story. Same pattern as the other chapter trophies: play the chapter's missions in order and the trophy lands when the final mission ends. By this point in the story most activities and side strands are open, so it is a good moment to start ticking off the activity trophies in stage 2 of the roadmap.
steps: Play the story missions of Chapter 4 in order.
The trophy unlocks when the chapter's final mission completes.

trophies.name: You Gotta Know When to Get Off
trophies.missable_note: Tied to the final story mission. Whether the finale can be replayed is not yet checked in the game — finish the story and it is yours.
trophies.guide: Complete the final mission of the story. This is the last story beat: finish every chapter, play the finale to its end, and the gold trophy unlocks. It is the natural end of roadmap stage 1 — after it, the game is yours to clean up in free roam for activities, collectibles and 100% completion.
steps: Complete all four chapters.
Play the final mission to its end.

trophies.name: Trust
trophies.missable_note: Tied to a named story mission. Whether story missions can be replayed is not yet checked in the game — play it when it appears.
trophies.guide: Complete the story mission Breakfast Run. It unlocks as part of the main story — play the mission when it appears and finish it. The mission's exact place in the chapter order is not pinned down by the official description, so treat it as a story-progress trophy and let it come to you.
steps: Play the story until the mission Breakfast Run appears.
Complete the mission.

trophies.name: Break the Bank
trophies.missable_note: Tied to a named story mission. Whether story missions can be replayed is not yet checked in the game — play it when it appears.
trophies.guide: Complete the story mission The Cartel Heist. A heist mission in the main story: play it when it appears and finish it. Heist missions in GTA games usually come with a setup chain, so if it is not available yet, keep playing the story — the mission unlocks in order.
steps: Play the story until the mission The Cartel Heist appears.
Complete the mission and its setup chain if one is offered.

trophies.name: Family Matters
trophies.missable_note: Tied to a named story mission. Whether story missions can be replayed is not yet checked in the game — play it when it appears.
trophies.guide: Complete the story mission Child's Play. It unlocks in the main story — play the mission when it appears and finish it. The official description names only the mission, so there is no extra requirement beyond completing it.
steps: Play the story until the mission Child's Play appears.
Complete the mission.

trophies.name: DWNFALL
trophies.missable_note: Tied to a named story mission. Whether story missions can be replayed is not yet checked in the game — play it when it appears.
trophies.guide: Complete the story mission Headliners. It unlocks in the main story — play the mission when it appears and finish it. The name suggests a show or performance set-piece; whatever the mission turns out to be, the requirement is only to complete it.
steps: Play the story until the mission Headliners appears.
Complete the mission.

trophies.name: Hi-Jacked
trophies.missable_note: Tied to a named story mission. Whether story missions can be replayed is not yet checked in the game — play it when it appears.
trophies.guide: Complete the story mission VCIA Takedown. VCIA is the Vice City International Airport area, so expect an airport set-piece. Play the mission when it appears in the story and finish it — the trophy is for completion only.
steps: Play the story until the mission VCIA Takedown appears.
Complete the mission.

trophies.name: Snow Storm
trophies.missable_note: Tied to a named story mission. Whether story missions can be replayed is not yet checked in the game — play it when it appears.
trophies.guide: Complete the story mission Operation Savage Glory. The operation name suggests a large coordinated mission; play it when it appears in the story and finish it. No extra condition is named in the official description — completion is the whole requirement.
steps: Play the story until the mission Operation Savage Glory appears.
Complete the mission.

trophies.name: A Long Road
trophies.missable_note: Not missable. 100% completion can be chased in free roam after the story; nothing in the official description is one-time-only.
trophies.guide: Reach 100% completion in the in-game stats. This is the long cleanup trophy and the last gold before the platinum: it counts story missions, activities, collectibles and the other completion categories the game tracks. Work through this guide's roadmap — story, activities, collectibles — and check the in-game stats screen to see which categories are still short. The exact list of what counts toward 100% is not spelled out in the official description, so use the stats screen as the source of truth and treat any category total as not yet checked until players confirm it.
steps: Finish the story and all named story missions.
Complete the activities, stranger strands and challenges in this guide.
Collect every card set, WAiNK spot and discovery, then check the stats screen for the remaining percentage.

trophies.name: Road to Rehabilitation
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Andy.
trophies.missable_note: Tied to the final mission of a character's strand. Whether strand missions can be replayed is not yet checked in the game — play the strand through when it opens.
trophies.guide: Complete the final mission for Andy. Andy is one of the characters with a mission strand: play their missions as they appear and finish the last one. The official description names only the endpoint, so the practical advice is to take Andy's missions whenever they are offered rather than leaving the strand for later.
steps: Take Andy's missions as they appear in the story.
Complete the final mission of the strand.

trophies.name: This Was No Boat Accident
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Kenton.
trophies.missable_note: Tied to the final mission of a character's strand. Whether strand missions can be replayed is not yet checked in the game — play the strand through when it opens.
trophies.guide: Complete the final mission for Kenton. Play Kenton's mission strand as it opens and finish the last mission. The boat-accident name hints at the strand's theme, but the requirement is only completion — take the missions when offered and the trophy follows.
steps: Take Kenton's missions as they appear in the story.
Complete the final mission of the strand.

trophies.name: The Lone Rider
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Billy.
trophies.missable_note: Tied to the final mission of a character's strand. Whether strand missions can be replayed is not yet checked in the game — play the strand through when it opens.
trophies.guide: Complete the final mission for Billy. Play Billy's mission strand as it opens and finish the last mission. The lone-rider name suggests a solo ride or bike theme, but the trophy only asks for completion of the strand's finale.
steps: Take Billy's missions as they appear in the story.
Complete the final mission of the strand.

trophies.name: Supply & Demand
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Randy.
trophies.missable_note: Tied to the final mission of a character's strand. Whether strand missions can be replayed is not yet checked in the game — play the strand through when it opens.
trophies.guide: Complete the final mission for Randy. Play Randy's mission strand as it opens and finish the last mission. The name suggests a supply-run theme; the trophy itself only requires the strand's finale to be completed.
steps: Take Randy's missions as they appear in the story.
Complete the final mission of the strand.

trophies.name: Spin On This!
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Tyrone.
trophies.missable_note: Tied to the final mission of a character's strand. Whether strand missions can be replayed is not yet checked in the game — play the strand through when it opens.
trophies.guide: Complete the final mission for Tyrone. Play Tyrone's mission strand as it opens and finish the last mission. Five character strands have a finale trophy each (Andy, Kenton, Billy, Randy, Tyrone) — clearing a strand when it is offered keeps all five moving together.
steps: Take Tyrone's missions as they appear in the story.
Complete the final mission of the strand.

trophies.name: Strangers & Freaks
trophies.description: Complete 8 mission strands for strangers across the state of Leonida.
trophies.missable_note: Not missable. Stranger strands stay available in free roam; the count is what matters, not the order.
trophies.guide: Complete 8 mission strands for strangers across Leonida. Strangers are the question-mark characters you meet out in the world — each has a short strand of missions. Eight strands must be finished, so explore the map, take every stranger mission you find, and finish each strand to its end. The five named character finales (Andy, Kenton, Billy, Randy, Tyrone) are their own trophies; the stranger strands here are the separate world encounters. Which strangers exist and where they appear is not yet checked in the game, so use the map markers and take every strand you meet.
steps: Explore Leonida and take stranger missions wherever they appear.
Finish each strand to its final mission.
Repeat until 8 strands are complete.

trophies.name: Actions Speak Louder
trophies.missable_note: The description is cryptic and the trigger is not yet checked in the game. Treat story choice moments as one-time until replay is confirmed.
trophies.guide: The official description is only: choices made (for better or worse). The honest reading is that this is a story-choice trophy — a moment where you pick between options and the game records the choice. Which choice, and whether it can be redone, is not yet checked in the game, so do not guess at a specific mission. Play the story, make the choices as they come, and check the sources below for player findings once they are pinned down.
steps: Play the story and make choices as they are offered.
Exact trigger not yet checked in the game — see the cited sources for the latest player findings.

trophies.name: Bad Luck, I Guess
trophies.missable_note: The description is cryptic and the trigger is not yet checked in the game. Treat story moments as one-time until replay is confirmed.
trophies.guide: The official description is only: second time's the charm. The honest reading is that this unlocks on a retry — a second attempt at something that failed the first time, most likely a story mission or challenge. Which attempt it is has not yet been checked in the game, so there is no reliable specific advice yet. If you fail a mission, retry it rather than reloading an old save — that is the behaviour the description points at.
steps: If a mission or challenge fails, retry it instead of reloading an older save.
Exact trigger not yet checked in the game — see the cited sources for the latest player findings.

trophies.name: The Truth Is Out There
trophies.missable_note: The description is cryptic and the trigger is not yet checked in the game. Treat story moments as one-time until replay is confirmed.
trophies.guide: The official description is only: what the hell just happened? The honest reading is that this is tied to a surprising story beat or easter-egg moment — the kind of scene players talk about afterwards. Which scene it is has not yet been checked in the game, so do not chase a specific location. Play the story and the side content, and check the sources below once players pin the trigger down.
steps: Play the story and side content as normal.
Exact trigger not yet checked in the game — see the cited sources for the latest player findings.

trophies.name: Personal Best
trophies.missable_note: The description is cryptic and the trigger is not yet checked in the game. Treat story moments as one-time until replay is confirmed.
trophies.guide: The official description is only: a partnership with mass appeal. The honest reading is that this involves the central partnership — Lucia and Jason — and something the pair does together that draws a crowd or a following. What exactly it counts has not yet been checked in the game, so there is no reliable specific advice yet. Play the story with both protagonists and check the sources below once players pin the trigger down.
steps: Play the story with both protagonists.
Exact trigger not yet checked in the game — see the cited sources for the latest player findings.

trophies.name: Cunning Stunts
trophies.missable_note: Not missable. Stunts can be repeated any time in free roam; only the count matters.
trophies.guide: Complete 250 stunts. Stunts are the jumps, near-misses, airtime and trick driving the game counts as you drive — the counter climbs in normal play, faster if you deliberately use ramps and jumps. This is a grind trophy, not a skill gate: 250 is a lot, but every stunt counts and nothing is one-time. Drive aggressively between missions and the total grows on its own; for the last stretch, chain jumps off ramps in the same area.
steps: Drive fast and use ramps, jumps and airtime whenever you travel.
Track the stunt count in the stats screen.
Grind the remainder with repeated ramp jumps in free roam.

trophies.name: Master of None
trophies.description: Try each type of activity once.
trophies.missable_note: Not missable. Activities stay available in free roam; you only need one attempt at each type.
trophies.guide: Try each type of activity once. This is a sampler trophy: play one round of every activity the game offers — races, shooting range, fishing, bowling, arcade games, drone races, meditation spots and the rest. You do not need to win or complete any of them, only to try each type. The full list of activity types is not spelled out in the official description, so work through the activities named by the other trophies in this guide and try anything else the map offers. If a type is unclear, the stats or activities screen is the source of truth for what counts.
steps: Try one of each activity: race, shooting range, fishing, bowling, arcade, drone race, meditation.
Try any other activity the map offers.
The trophy unlocks when every type has been attempted once.

trophies.name: The Shootist
trophies.description: Earn a gold medal in all Shooting Range challenges.
trophies.missable_note: Not missable. Shooting Range challenges can be retried any time; gold is a score target, not a one-time window.
trophies.guide: Earn a gold medal in all Shooting Range challenges. Head to a shooting range and work through every challenge, aiming for the gold score in each. This is the one pure-skill trophy in the set: use the range's own scoring feedback, retry freely, and learn each challenge's target layout before going for gold. The number of challenges and their gold thresholds are not spelled out in the official description, so use the range's own challenge list as the source of truth.
steps: Visit a Shooting Range and open its challenge list.
Complete each challenge, then retry for the gold medal score.
Repeat until every challenge shows gold.

trophies.name: Top Fun
trophies.description: Win a Top Fun Drone Race at every location.
trophies.missable_note: Not missable. Drone races can be retried at every location; only a win at each one counts.
trophies.guide: Win a Top Fun Drone Race at every location. Find each drone-race location on the map, enter the race and win it — one win per location, all locations required. Drone races are a learned skill: fly the course once to learn the gates, then race for the win. How many locations exist is not spelled out in the official description, so use the map's race markers as the source of truth and clear each one.
steps: Find every Top Fun Drone Race location on the map.
Enter each race and win it.
Repeat until every location has a win.

trophies.name: Earn Cash, Not Kudos
trophies.missable_note: Not missable. Races can be retried; only wins at 20 different races count.
trophies.guide: Win 20 different races. The key word is different: winning the same race twenty times does not count — you need a win at twenty separate races. Work through the race markers across the map, one win each. Short races are the fastest to clear, so start with those and use the map to avoid repeating a race you have already won.
steps: Find race markers across the map.
Win one race at each of 20 different races.
Use the map to avoid repeating a race already won.

trophies.name: Baited My Tackle
trophies.description: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge.
trophies.missable_note: Not missable. Fishing challenges can be retried; the requirement is one win against Cal.
trophies.guide: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge. Cal is a fishing rival you meet through the fishing activity — take the challenge against him and out-fish him. Fishing challenges are usually scored on catch size or count, so learn the fishing controls in a free session first, then take Cal on. If the challenge is not offered yet, keep fishing and progressing the activity until Cal appears.
steps: Try the fishing activity to learn the controls.
Take the fishing challenge against Cal when it is offered.
Out-fish Cal to win the challenge.

trophies.name: Stick Fiddler
trophies.missable_note: Not missable. Arcade games can be played any time; completing one is enough.
trophies.guide: Complete an arcade game. Find an arcade machine — in an arcade, a bar or wherever the game places them — and play a game through to its end. Any arcade game counts, and you do not need a high score: finishing one game is the whole requirement. Which arcade games exist and where the machines are is not yet checked in the game, so look for arcade markers and try the first machine you find.
steps: Find an arcade machine.
Play one arcade game through to its end.

trophies.name: Positive Mental Attitude
trophies.description: Meditate at every spot across Leonida.
trophies.missable_note: Not missable. Meditation spots stay available; you need one session at each spot.
trophies.guide: Meditate at every spot across Leonida. Meditation spots are quiet places marked in the world — visit each one and complete a meditation session. The total number of spots is not spelled out in the official description, so use the map's markers as the source of truth and work through them area by area. This pairs well with The Goodtime State, since both reward covering the whole map.
steps: Find meditation spots on the map.
Complete one meditation session at each spot.
Work area by area until every spot is done.

trophies.name: Fair Game
trophies.description: Hunt a unique animal for Bret.
trophies.missable_note: Not missable. The hunt can be retried; the requirement is one unique animal for Bret.
trophies.guide: Hunt a unique animal for Bret. Bret is a hunting contact: take the hunt he offers, track the unique animal and take it down. Unique animals are one-of-a-kind targets, so follow the hunt's own trail markers rather than hunting at random. Where Bret is found and which animal he wants is not yet checked in the game, so take the hunt when it is offered and follow its guidance.
steps: Find Bret and take the hunt he offers.
Follow the hunt's trail to the unique animal.
Take the animal down to complete the hunt.

trophies.name: One Last Thing
trophies.missable_note: Not missable. Challenges are a running count across activities; nothing is one-time-only.
trophies.guide: Complete 50 challenges. Challenges are the small objectives attached to activities — race targets, stunt goals, shooting-range scores and the like — and the counter climbs across all of them. This is a volume trophy: play the activities, take the challenges they offer, and 50 will arrive in normal play. If you are short near the end, the challenges screen shows which activity types still have open challenges.
steps: Play activities and take the challenges they offer.
Check the challenges screen for open ones.
Complete challenges until the count reaches 50.

trophies.name: Hot Together
trophies.description: Lose a 4 star Wanted Level with your partner and escape the heat.
trophies.missable_note: Not missable. Wanted levels can be raised and escaped any time in free roam with your partner.
trophies.guide: Lose a 4-star Wanted Level with your partner and escape the heat. Build your wanted level to 4 stars while your partner is with you, then break line of sight and stay out of the search area until the heat dies. The practical approach: cause chaos in an open area with good escape routes, watch the wanted stars climb to 4, then hide — in a building, a tunnel or off-road — until the stars clear. Doing it with your partner present is the requirement, so start it from a mission or moment when they are with you.
steps: Make sure your partner is with you.
Raise your Wanted Level to 4 stars.
Break line of sight and hide until the stars clear.

trophies.name: Retail Therapy
trophies.description: Rob 3 shops back-to-back with your partner without losing your Wanted Level.
trophies.missable_note: Not missable. Shop robberies can be retried in free roam with your partner.
trophies.guide: Rob 3 shops back-to-back with your partner without losing your Wanted Level. The trick is the back-to-back part: hit three shops in a row, keeping the same wanted level through all three — do not lose the cops between robberies, and do not let the level rise or fall in a way that breaks the chain. Plan a route with three close shops, rob quickly, move to the next, and only escape after the third. If the chain breaks, retry — it costs nothing but time.
steps: Make sure your partner is with you.
Pick a route with three close shops.
Rob all three in a row without losing your Wanted Level, then escape.

trophies.name: Gunslinger
trophies.description: Take down 5 enemies in a single use of Combat Focus.
trophies.missable_note: Not missable. Combat Focus can be used any time in combat; retry freely.
trophies.guide: Take down 5 enemies in a single use of Combat Focus. Combat Focus is the slow-time aiming mode: trigger it in a fight with at least five enemies close together and drop all five before it ends. The best setup is a mission or encounter with a group of enemies in the open — wait until they are clustered, trigger Combat Focus, and work through them quickly. If you run out of targets, retry in the next big fight.
steps: Find a fight with at least five enemies clustered together.
Trigger Combat Focus.
Take down five enemies before it ends.

trophies.name: Catch Me If You Can
trophies.description: Make an unscheduled departure at VCIA.
trophies.missable_note: Not missable. VCIA is open in free roam; an unscheduled departure can be attempted any time.
trophies.guide: Make an unscheduled departure at VCIA (Vice City International Airport). The honest reading is: get a plane off the ground from the airport without going through a scheduled flight — take a plane from the runway and leave. Which aircraft counts and whether the police response matters is not yet checked in the game, so try the straightforward approach first: enter the airport, take a plane, and take off. If that does not trigger it, check the sources below for player findings.
steps: Go to VCIA, the airport.
Take a plane and make an unscheduled departure — take off without a scheduled flight.
Exact trigger not yet checked in the game — see the cited sources for the latest player findings.

trophies.name: Challenging Tank
trophies.missable_note: Not missable. Rhino tanks can be found and driven in free roam; the requirement is not one-time-only.
trophies.guide: The official description is only: kinda hot in these Rhinos. The honest reading is that this involves the Rhino tank — driving one, or surviving in one while the heat is on. Where a Rhino is found and what exactly triggers the trophy is not yet checked in the game, so do not guess at a specific spot. Find a Rhino tank, drive it, and cause enough chaos for the game to notice; check the sources below once players pin the trigger down.
steps: Find a Rhino tank.
Drive it and draw heat.
Exact trigger not yet checked in the game — see the cited sources for the latest player findings.

trophies.name: Sneakthief
trophies.description: Rob a jewelry store without being detected.
trophies.missable_note: Not missable. Jewelry stores can be robbed again in free roam; retry until undetected.
trophies.guide: Rob a jewelry store without being detected. This is a stealth robbery: enter the store, take the goods, and leave without any alarm or detection. Go in quiet — avoid cameras and staff sightlines, move fast, and leave before anyone reacts. If you are spotted, the attempt fails the trophy, so retry: the store can be robbed again. The exact detection rules are not spelled out in the official description, so treat any alarm as a failed attempt and try a quieter approach.
steps: Pick a jewelry store.
Enter quietly, avoid cameras and staff sightlines.
Take the goods and leave without being detected.

trophies.name: Maximum Withdrawal
trophies.missable_note: Not missable. Bank vaults can be robbed repeatedly in free roam; only five successful escapes count.
trophies.guide: Rob 5 bank vaults and escape. Five separate vault robberies, each ending in a clean escape. Vaults are the big robberies: plan the approach, hit the vault, then lose the wanted level before the next one. The count is cumulative, so you can space them out across your playthrough. Which banks hold vaults and how vault robberies start is not yet checked in the game — use the robbery opportunities the world offers and count your escapes.
steps: Find and rob a bank vault.
Escape the wanted level.
Repeat until five vaults have been robbed and escaped from.

trophies.name: A Classic Blitz Play
trophies.description: Rob an Armored Truck and escape.
trophies.missable_note: Not missable. Armored trucks appear in free roam; rob one and escape, retry freely.
trophies.guide: Rob an armored truck and escape. Armored trucks drive the roads of Leonida — spot one, stop it, take the cash and lose the wanted level. The classic blitz approach is to block the truck's path, force it to stop, and hit it fast before backup arrives. Trucks appear in traffic, so this is a free-roam trophy: keep an eye out while driving and strike when you see one.
steps: Spot an armored truck on the road.
Stop it and take the cash.
Escape the wanted level.

trophies.name: Pest Control
trophies.description: Rob an Illegal Operation belonging to each gang.
trophies.missable_note: Not missable. Illegal operations stay available in free roam; you need one per gang.
trophies.guide: Rob an illegal operation belonging to each gang. Leonida's gangs run illegal operations around the map — hit one operation per gang, not several from the same gang. The trophy is about coverage: one robbery for every gang in the game. Which gangs exist and where their operations are is not yet checked in the game, so use the world's robbery markers and keep a note of which gangs you have already hit.
steps: Find illegal operations on the map.
Rob one operation for each gang.
Repeat until every gang has been hit once.

trophies.name: In The Beginning…
trophies.description: Enjoy a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach.
trophies.missable_note: Not missable. Ocean Beach is open in free roam; the cocktail moment can be done any time.
trophies.guide: Enjoy a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach. Head to Ocean Beach, find the bar or spot with the view, and order the cocktail. This is a small flavour trophy — a quiet moment, not a challenge. The exact spot is not pinned down by the official description, so look for a beachfront bar on Ocean Beach and take the cocktail option when it is offered.
steps: Go to Ocean Beach.
Find the beachfront bar with the view.
Order and enjoy the cocktail.

trophies.name: Capital Offense
trophies.description: Smash your way out of a vehicle showroom in classic style.
trophies.missable_note: Not missable. Showrooms can be smashed again in free roam; retry freely.
trophies.guide: Smash your way out of a vehicle showroom in classic style. The classic style is the GTA signature move: drive a car straight through the showroom glass and out the other side. Pick a vehicle showroom, get a car inside or drive one in, then smash out through the front. Which showroom counts and whether any car works is not yet checked in the game, so try the straightforward approach first and check the sources below if it does not trigger.
steps: Find a vehicle showroom.
Get a car and smash your way out through the glass, in classic style.
Exact trigger not yet checked in the game — see the cited sources for the latest player findings.

trophies.name: Let’s Go Bowling
trophies.description: Follow-through at the Kolt & Associates' bowling alley.
trophies.missable_note: Not missable. The bowling alley stays open; follow-through can be done any time.
trophies.guide: Follow-through at the Kolt & Associates' bowling alley. Go to the bowling alley and bowl a game — follow-through means completing the delivery, so play a frame through rather than walking away mid-game. The alley is the named location, so this is a visit-and-play trophy, not a score trophy: bowl and the trophy follows.
steps: Go to the Kolt & Associates' bowling alley.
Play a game of bowling and follow through on your delivery.

trophies.name: Ten Pin
trophies.description: Bowl 'em over with a melee drive-by.
trophies.missable_note: Not missable. Melee drive-bys can be attempted any time in free roam; retry freely.
trophies.guide: Bowl them over with a melee drive-by. A drive-by with a melee weapon — strike pedestrians or targets from a moving vehicle with a bat or similar weapon, bowling them over. The name is a bowling pun: the target is to knock people down like pins. Do it from a moving vehicle with a melee weapon equipped. How many knockdowns it takes is not spelled out in the official description, so keep at it until the trophy pops.
steps: Get a vehicle and equip a melee weapon.
Perform a melee drive-by, knocking targets over.
Repeat until the trophy unlocks.

trophies.name: Dime on the Dollar
trophies.description: Earn $250,000 laundering Marked Bills through your contacts.
trophies.missable_note: Not missable. Marked Bills can be laundered over time through contacts; only the $250,000 total matters.
trophies.guide: Earn $250,000 laundering Marked Bills through your contacts. Marked Bills are the dirty cash you pick up from robberies and heists — they cannot be spent directly, so launder them through your contacts to turn them into clean money. The $250,000 is cumulative, so keep laundering as you earn. Which contacts launder bills and what cut they take is not yet checked in the game, so use the contacts the game offers for laundering and watch the total climb.
steps: Earn Marked Bills from robberies and heists.
Launder them through your contacts.
Repeat until $250,000 has been laundered.

trophies.name: Treat Yo Self
trophies.missable_note: Not missable. Spending is cumulative across all shops; buy over time in free roam.
trophies.guide: Spend $100,000 across all shops. The total is cumulative and counts every shop in the game — clothes, weapons, food, car mods, whatever you buy. This is a money trophy, not a shopping list: earn cash through missions and robberies, then spend it. If you are short near the end, buy the big-ticket items — vehicles and weapon upgrades move the total fastest. The count is across all shops combined, so no single shop needs $100,000.
steps: Earn cash through missions, robberies and activities.
Spend it across any shops.
Repeat until $100,000 has been spent in total.

trophies.name: On the Spot
trophies.description: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app.
trophies.missable_note: Not missable. Vehicles can be registered any time in free roam; only the count of 10 matters.
trophies.guide: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app. The Scooter Bros app is the in-game vehicle service — open it and register vehicles you find or own, one by one, until ten are registered. Any ten vehicles count, so register the ones you drive past or own already. Where the app lives in the phone menu and whether a vehicle must be owned first is not yet checked in the game, so open the app and follow its own prompts.
steps: Open the Scooter Bros app on the in-game phone.
Register a vehicle.
Repeat until 10 vehicles are registered.

trophies.name: Don't Touch My Deck
trophies.missable_note: Not missable. Cards stay in the world in free roam; collect sets at your own pace.
trophies.guide: Complete 3 collectible card sets. Collectible cards are hidden around Leonida, grouped into sets — finish three full sets to unlock this. Cards are a search trophy: sweep each area carefully, check the usual hiding places (alleys, rooftops, interiors, landmarks), and track which sets are still short. How many cards are in a set and where they hide is not yet checked in the game, so use the in-game collection screen as the source of truth and collect methodically.
steps: Find collectible cards around Leonida.
Track sets on the in-game collection screen.
Complete three full sets.

trophies.name: You WAiNKer!
trophies.missable_note: Not missable. WAiNK spots stay available in free roam; the count of 100 is cumulative.
trophies.guide: WAiNK It at 100 locations. WAiNK is the in-game social or tagging activity — find its 100 locations across Leonida and use it at each one. This is the biggest count in the collectible set, so treat it as a map-coverage task: work area by area and let the counter climb as you travel. What WAiNK It actually does at a location is not yet checked in the game, so follow the activity's own prompt when a location offers it.
steps: Find WAiNK locations across Leonida.
WAiNK It at each one.
Work area by area until the count reaches 100.

trophies.name: The Goodtime State
trophies.missable_note: Not missable. Exploration is cumulative; every corner of the map counts whenever you reach it.
trophies.guide: Explore all of Leonida. Visit every named area of the state — Vice City, the beaches, the Keys, the swamps, the farmland and the small towns in between. The trophy is for map coverage: drive, fly and walk into every corner until the map is filled in. Pair it with the other coverage trophies (meditation spots, WAiNK locations, vehicle discoveries) and let one long road trip knock out several at once. The exact list of areas is not spelled out in the official description, so use the map itself as the source of truth.
steps: Open the map and note the unexplored areas.
Travel to every named area of Leonida.
Repeat until the whole state is explored.

trophies.name: Whip It Good
trophies.missable_note: Not missable. Vehicle discoveries are cumulative; any 100 vehicles count.
trophies.guide: Discover 100 vehicles. Every new vehicle type you drive or enter counts toward the total — cars, bikes, boats, planes, whatever the game counts as a vehicle. This climbs naturally if you vary what you drive: take a different vehicle each time you travel instead of sticking to one favourite. The count is of discoveries, so repeats do not help — variety is the strategy. Which vehicles the game counts is not spelled out in the official description, so use the in-game vehicle or stats screen as the source of truth.
steps: Drive a wide variety of vehicles — cars, bikes, boats, planes.
Take a different vehicle each time you travel.
Repeat until 100 vehicles have been discovered.

trophies.name: Little Boxes
trophies.missable_note: Not missable. Garage properties stay for sale in free roam; buy them whenever you can afford them.
trophies.guide: Purchase all garage properties. Garages are the properties that store your vehicles — buy every one the game offers. They cost money, so this pairs with the money-making trophies: earn cash, then buy garages as they become available. How many garages exist and what they cost is not yet checked in the game, so watch for property-for-sale markers and buy each garage when it appears.
steps: Earn cash through missions and activities.
Watch for garage properties for sale.
Purchase every garage property.
